title: Constant-factor approximation for Dasgupta’s hierarchical clustering objective
area: Approximation algorithms and hardness of approximation
formal: Do there exist real constants \(C\ge1\), \(K>0\), an integer \(a\ge1\), and one deterministic multitape Turing machine which, on every explicitly encoded nonnegative rational similarity graph \(G\), outputs a hierarchy \(T\) with \(\operatorname{cost}_G(T)\le C\operatorname{OPT}(G)\) within \(K(N+1)^a\) bit operations, where \(N\) is the total input bit length and the cost and allowed hierarchies are defined below?
definitions:
An input is an integer \(n\ge2\) and a finite simple undirected graph \(G=([n],E,w)\), where \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(E\subseteq\{\{u,v\}:1\le u<v\le n\}\), and \(w:E\to\mathbb Q_{\ge0}\). The encoding explicitly lists all \(n\) vertices, including isolated ones, and all edges with their endpoints and weights. Integers use ordinary binary notation with delimiters; each rational weight is a nonnegative integer numerator and positive integer denominator in binary. The explicit vertex list ensures \(N\ge n\). There are no loops or repeated edges. An absent edge has weight zero. The graph need not be connected and has no metric, clusterability, density or sampling promise.

A hierarchy is a finite rooted full binary tree whose leaves are labeled bijectively by \([n]\); every internal node has exactly two children. For a node \(z\), let \(L_T(z)\subseteq[n]\) be its descendant leaf labels. For distinct leaves \(u,v\), let \(\operatorname{lca}_T(u,v)\) be their least common ancestor. Define
\[
\operatorname{cost}_G(T)=\sum_{\{u,v\}\in E}w(\{u,v\})\,|L_T(\operatorname{lca}_T(u,v))|,
\qquad
\operatorname{OPT}(G)=\min_T\operatorname{cost}_G(T).
\]
Each unordered edge contributes once. The minimum is over all such trees, with no restriction on height or balance. The output explicitly lists the root, child edges and leaf labels of one tree. If all weights are zero, the required cost is zero and any valid hierarchy qualifies.

The same finite machine and constants must work for every \(n\), graph and weight encoding. All input reads, binary arithmetic, preprocessing and output writes count in the worst-case running time. The machine has no random bits, advice, external comparison or cluster-label oracle, or uncharged preprocessing. The factor \(C\) is independent of \(n\), the number of edges and the sizes or ratios of the weights; it is not an input parameter. Only the tree is required as output, and its stated cost guarantee is mathematical, using exact rational weights.

context_blocks.text: The source defines a cost for a complete hierarchy of pairwise similarities. This card retains the previously selected deterministic polynomial-time, constant-factor question. The explicit rational encoding and vertex list fix bit complexity and output size; they do not impose a structural promise.

The general approximation guarantee of Charikar and Chatziafratis is \(O(\sqrt{\log n})\). Their Theorem 3.4 proves Small-Set-Expansion hardness of approximation within every constant factor, already on unweighted graphs. This is a conditional complexity barrier, not an unconditional proof that the requested machine cannot exist.
The ICALP 2025 sublinear result assumes a clusterable graph and access to cluster labels of sampled seeds. Its input model and guarantee do not supply the unrestricted algorithm asked for here.

The July 2026 generalized clustering paper permits a leaf cluster to remain a whole graph from a specified class, such as a tree. Its objective can consequently vanish on inputs for which singleton-leaf hierarchies have positive cost. Those results concern a different stopping rule.

A constant-factor guarantee for the complementary revenue-maximization objective does not, just from that guarantee, give a constant-factor bound for this minimization objective. The target here is the displayed cost itself.

why: A hierarchy must represent similarity at every scale, so optimizing a single flat partition is insufficient. A constant approximation for this canonical objective would give a uniform quality guarantee on arbitrary similarity data and would cross a major graph-partitioning hardness barrier.
answer_criterion: Supply a complete mathematically correct Lean proof of the existence of a machine and fixed constants satisfying every stated guarantee, or a complete Lean proof of their nonexistence. An approximation factor growing with the input size, a result for a promised graph class, or a guarantee with an additional oracle does not settle this target. A conditional hardness result establishes its implication but does not by itself prove the unconditional negative answer.

sentences: The input is an arbitrary graph whose nonnegative edge weights express pairwise similarities.
A hierarchy repeatedly separates its vertices until every leaf contains one vertex.
An edge pays its weight times the size of the smallest cluster containing both endpoints.
The question asks for one deterministic polynomial-time algorithm with a fixed approximation factor on every such graph.
Known general guarantees grow with the number of vertices, while Small-Set-Expansion hardness and results for richer inputs or different objectives do not unconditionally settle this question.
